entities.summary:
Osasco is a municipality in the state of São Paulo, Brazil, located in the western portion of the Greater São Paulo metropolitan area. With approximately 750,000 people in 64.9 km², Osasco is one of Brazil's most densely populated cities and the fifth-largest municipality in São Paulo state. Once an industrial heartland known as the 'Manchester of Brazil,' Osasco has undergone significant economic transformation from manufacturing toward services and financial industries.

Originally a district of São Paulo municipality, Osasco became an independent municipality in 1962 after a populist campaign led by Adherbal Jurema, later known as Chico Jurema. The city's rapid industrialization in the 1950s–1970s made it a center of the ABC Paulista labor movement — the workers' strikes of 1968 in Osasco's Cobrasma metalworking plant were among the first major labor actions against Brazil's military dictatorship. Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who became Brazil's president (2003–2011 and 2023–), worked as a metalworker in the Greater São Paulo industrial region and was shaped by this labor movement tradition.

Osasco today is home to Banco Bradesco, one of Brazil's largest private banks, and has become a significant financial and service center within Greater São Paulo. The city represents the broader story of Brazilian industrial workers' rights activism under authoritarian rule, the rise of the Workers' Party (PT) out of the ABC industrial labor movement, and the transformation of Brazilian cities from industrial to service economies in the late 20th century.
